requirements.text: Conformance claims MUST use the normative terminology and RFC-2119-style language defined in SES-000; undefined terms MUST NOT be relied upon to establish conformance.
Trust domains MUST be explicit and lower-trust input MUST NOT create authority.
Execution MUST follow the canonical lifecycle or an equivalent state-machine trace.
Semantic meaning MUST derive from an authoritative semantic contract.
Security- and meaning-relevant operations MUST have canonical graph identity.
Rewrites MUST preserve declared semantics under explicit algebraic preconditions.
Resolution MUST be deterministic or deterministically abstain on ambiguity.
Traversal MUST enforce semantic scope and bounded resource consumption.
Authorization MUST evaluate the fully resolved operation graph in trusted context.
Authorization provenance MUST bind semantics, policy, and validity to executable artifacts.
Planning MUST NOT widen authorized semantics.
Execution IR MUST be independently validated before crossing the provider boundary.
Provider execution MUST satisfy declared semantic and security fidelity requirements.
Mutation profiles MUST specify atomicity, idempotency, replay, concurrency, and failure behavior.
Plan caching MUST never substitute stale or broader authority for current authorization.
All transports and agents MUST converge on equivalent semantic and authorization behavior.
Semantic resource amplification MUST be bounded by enforceable budgets.
Evidence MUST reconstruct security lineage without becoming an authority source.
Generated metadata MUST be reproducible, version-bound, and semantically equivalent to its source.
Every backlog item in the future development roadmap MUST be tracked with a stable identifier and an explicit status in a machine-readable gap registry until it is resolved or formally deferred.
Security- and meaning-relevant artifacts MUST conform to the formal data model's typed schema and stated invariants.
Lifecycle and security-relevant state transitions MUST be representable in the defined state machines, with no reachable undefined transition.
Cross-transport exchange of semantic artifacts MUST use the transport-neutral wire protocol, or an encoding independently verified equivalent to it.
Independently evolving implementations MUST negotiate compatibility using the defined versioning rules before exchanging semantic artifacts.
Delegated or attenuated authority MUST be representable in the authority algebra and independently verifiable at the point of use.
Providers MUST declare a capability/fidelity profile, and that profile MUST be independently verifiable against observed execution behavior.
Security- and semantic-relevant claims MUST be independently verifiable via a defined proof or attestation format.
Every normative requirement MUST map to independent validation and explicit conformance status.

Every conformance test MUST declare its fixture and oracle, and at least one independent oracle class MUST be used for security-critical semantic, authorization, rewrite, and provider-fidelity requirements.
Every normative requirement MUST have a traceability record with an explicit status, and CI MUST reject a release when an applicable critical requirement is Missing or Implemented/unproven.
Every declared security boundary MUST have adversarial conformance coverage before a profile can claim that boundary is enforced.
The repository MUST maintain a machine-readable gap file mapping every backlog item and requirement to an explicit, current status.
Portable vectors MUST encode both successful and fail-closed expected outcomes.
Reference implementations MUST remain informative and disclose deviations from the normative standard.
